blockers.summary: GET /archive has no owned path; 00-FOUNDATION §7 assigns apps/api/archive/** to nobody, so the handler is mounted at /api/v1/schedule/archive
no alert_deliveries table, so notification dedupe cannot be persisted; the delivery log is in-memory and a restart or second instance can double-send
no shared home for the response envelope or display formatters; the envelope sits in apps/api/schedule/lib/http.ts and formatCountdown is duplicated in the web layer
users has no timezone column, so a notification cannot reliably state the start time in the recipient's own zone
tracks has no variant relation or version label, so Which mix? infers pairs from version suffixes in titles
the ICS feed, the no-login unsubscribe and the delivery tick are required by 05-AGENT-C but absent from the API contract
Agent A's BroadcastContext path and shape, and Agent B's auth() module, are guesses; imports are written unresolved rather than mocked
cannot add next-mdx-remote because apps/web/package.json is not owned and does not exist
no table for web push subscription endpoint and keys, so the web_push channel the contract permits cannot be delivered to
the staff editor required by C4 cannot save; the contract lists only the two post read endpoints
no contract endpoint for reading a game pair; only POST /games/:slug/events is specified
the schedule cannot be the homepage; apps/web/app/page.tsx and next.config are not owned by Agent C
alert settings has no owned address; app/(account)/** belongs to Agent B, so it is mounted at /schedule/alerts
apps/api/posts/** and apps/api/games/** are in Agent C's write list in 05-AGENT-C but not in the ownership table in 00-FOUNDATION §7

env_vars_note: Could not be written to .env.example: that file is repository-root shared infrastructure and is not in Agent C's ownership table. Every variable is documented in SUBMISSION.md §8.
dependencies_note: Declared, not installed. apps/web/package.json is not owned by Agent C and does not exist; see blocker-9. No dependency was added for mail (the transport uses fetch) or for iCalendar (written by hand against RFC 5545).
screens_note: No screenshots exist. There is no app shell, no packages/ui, no seed and no dev server, so no screen has been rendered in either seed mode. Per 06-SUBMISSION-PROTOCOL §6, none of these screens are delivered.

no_personalised_ordering.how: No sort, filter or grouping function in the lane accepts a user identifier. GET /schedule reads no session and takes only a date range and a timezone. Ordering is a pure function of starts_at with an id tie-break, asserted by three tests in apps/api/schedule/lib/schedule.test.ts. listening_sessions is never read; game_events is read only to compute a public vote split identical for every viewer.
